name: Judeo-Tunisian Arabic

ancestors.notes: Judeo-Arabic macrolanguage node (ISO 639 jrb): a sociolinguistic/orthographic collective, not genetic descent (see jrb.json notes) -- ajt's single genetic PARENT is ar-TN, matching the engine constraint that every language has at most one PARENT ancestor.
Regional descent: Judeo-Tunisian Arabic is fundamentally a Tunisian Arabic dialect, historically written in Hebrew script.
Hebrew liturgical/lexical adstrate, shared with the rest of the Judeo-Arabic continuum (jrb.json).

notes: STUB. Judeo-Tunisian Arabic (ISO 639-3 ajt), the variety of Tunisian Arabic spoken and written (in Hebrew script) by Tunisian Jews. Per Wikipedia (Judeo-Tunisian Arabic) it differs phonologically from mainstream Tunisian Arabic in lacking the Banu Hilal/Banu Sulaym Bedouin dialect layer: it merges the glottal stop /ʔ/ and /h/, merges the interdental fricatives /θ ð/ with the dental stops /t d/, merges ḍ and ḍ̣ (ض/ظ) as /dˤ/, and retains the pre-Hilalian diphthongs /aw/ and /ay/ that mainstream (Hilalized) Tunisian Arabic monophthongised. These are real, citable phonological facts, but a complete letter-to-IPA grapheme table requires deciding the exact Hebrew-script orthographic conventions used for Judeo-Tunisian texts, which was not sourced with confidence this session (no JIPA illustration or dedicated phonology paper was fetched); rather than guess a Hebrew-script mapping, this spec is a metadata + notes-only stub. graphemes intentionally empty pending that sourcing pass. ISO STATUS NOTE (verified this session against iso639-3.sil.org): ajt is a RETIRED/deprecated ISO 639-3 code, merged into aeb (Tunisian Arabic) by change request 2021-020, effective 2022-01-20; Wikipedia's Judeo-Tunisian Arabic article confirms 'ajt subsumed in aeb Tunisian Arabic.' It is kept here as the requested language code per the batch spec (matching this repo's file-per-named-variety convention, parallel to how the jrb macrolanguage's member codes are modelled individually) but downstream consumers should be aware SIL/Ethnologue no longer list it as a live code; aeb.json (if present) is the standards-current target.
